title: Combine web and store orders and add the customer with the right join
objective_text: Combine DataFrames with unions and joins: unionByName, left and inner joins, and multi-key joins.
scenario: Web and store orders land in two bronze tables built by different teams, with the same columns in a different order. Sales wants one silver.orders table with every order and the customer's name. Customers are keyed by customer_id and region, because the same id was reused in each region.
engine_label: DuckDB's PySpark API on this PC (not Apache Spark)
starting_environment: Delta tables bronze.web_orders, bronze.store_orders and bronze.customers in the exercise folder, and a starter answer.py.
required: Every web and store order appears once, tagged with channel web or store.
Columns are matched by name, not position, when the two order tables are stacked.
customer_name comes from bronze.customers matched on customer_id and region; an order with no customer keeps its row with customer_name 'unknown'.
Write silver.orders with order_id, customer_id, region, channel, amount, customer_name, so that running the code again leaves the same table.

expected.description: silver.orders has 7 rows, orders 1 to 7, each once; order 7's customer_name is unknown.

verifies: Your PySpark stacks two tables by column name and left-joins on a two-column key, on the exercise data and on rows you haven't seen, on this PC.
Running it again leaves the same table.
does_not_verify: It doesn't run on Apache Spark or in a Databricks workspace, so it doesn't show how Spark plans the join (broadcast or shuffle) or how it performs on large tables.
hints: F.lit("web") makes a constant column: add it with withColumn("channel", ...) before stacking.
web.union(store) matches columns by position; the store table's columns are in another order. unionByName matches them by name.
Customer 100 exists in EU and in US. Join on both columns: on=["customer_id", "region"].
how="left" keeps order 7, whose customer isn't in bronze.customers; F.coalesce(F.col("name"), F.lit("unknown")) labels it.
Write with mode("overwrite") so a rerun replaces the table.
explanation: Tag each source with a literal channel column and stack them with unionByName, because union matches by position and the store table's columns are in another order. Then left-join customers on the full key, customer_id and region: an inner join would drop the order whose customer hasn't arrived, and a join on customer_id alone would match order 1 to both customer 100s and count it twice. Coalesce the missing name to 'unknown', select the columns, and overwrite silver.orders so a rerun can't double it.
troubleshooting: An error about types in a union, or regions in the order_id column: the union is by position; use unionByName.
Some orders appear twice: the join key is missing region.
Order 7 is missing: the join is inner; use a left join.
reset: Reset rebuilds the bronze tables from setup.sql, removes silver.orders and puts the starter back.
cleanup: Everything lives in this exercise's folder on this PC; Reset or removing the exercise deletes it. Nothing is created in any workspace.
